r.정치 구도: A new constitution in 2015 made Nepal a federal democratic republic with seven provinces. Before that, a Maoist insurgency fought government forces for a decade from 1996, and after a 2006 peace deal the country abolished its 240-year-old monarchy in 2008. Since then the Nepali Congress and two communist parties have traded the prime minister's post by reshuffling coalitions, so governments have rarely lasted long. In September 2025, a government ban on social media sent young people into the streets; the parliament building was set on fire, dozens were killed and the government fell. In the March 2026 election, voters who had turned away from the old parties flocked to the new Rastriya Swatantra Party, which won 182 of 275 seats and formed a majority government. Rooting out corruption, creating jobs and stemming the exodus of young people abroad are the new government's biggest tasks.

t.why: As a landlocked country squeezed between India and China, keeping a balance without leaning toward either is the foundation of its foreign policy. Most goods and fuel arrive through India, so when cargo was stuck at the Indian border for months in 2015, the whole country ran short of fuel. Since then Nepal has expanded road and rail links with China, and in 2024 it signed a framework for cooperation under China's Belt and Road Initiative. It also has a long-running map dispute with India over the Kalapani and Lipulekh area in the northwest. Eight of the world's 14 peaks above 8,000 meters, Everest among them, are in Nepal, making it a magnet for climbers, and it is known for the Gurkha soldiers who serve in the British and Indian armies. It is often in the news as a front line of the climate crisis, where Himalayan glaciers are melting.
t.rel: A Himalayan landlocked country between India and China. It relies heavily on India for trade and supplies, while widening road and rail links with China to keep a balance.
t.korea: The two countries established diplomatic relations in 1974. Nepal is one of the largest sources of workers under South Korea's Employment Permit System, and more than 120,000 Nepalis have come to Korean factories and farms through it since 2008. In 2025 more than 100,000 people applied for a Korean-language test for 5,300 slots, a sign of how much a job in Korea means to young Nepalis. Money earned in Korea is sent home as remittances that support Nepal's economy. Korean mountaineers have mounted many Himalayan expeditions, building close ties with the Sherpas who climbed with them. There is also a Korean temple in Lumbini, the birthplace of the Buddha.
t.know: Nepal's flag is the only national flag in the world that is not a rectangle.
etext: So many people work abroad that money sent home exceeds a fifth of the economy. Earnings from the Gulf, Malaysia, South Korea and elsewhere prop up household spending, but they also reflect how few jobs there are at home.

Rivers pouring down from the Himalayas give Nepal huge hydropower potential. After years of chronic blackouts, new plants now let it sell surplus power to India and Bangladesh in the rainy season. In the dry season it still has to buy electricity from India, so adding storage-type plants that hold back water is the next challenge.

Everest climbing, trekking and pilgrimage sites such as Lumbini, the Buddha's birthplace, draw foreign visitors. Arrivals plunged after the 2015 earthquake, during COVID-19 and amid the 2025 protests, recovering each time.

With no coastline and most goods arriving through India, logistics are expensive. Manufacturing is weak, so imports far exceed exports, and remittances fill the gap. Frequent changes of government often delay big projects.
